exposure: abdominal subcutaneous adiposity (as measured by BMI and abdominal circumference)
outcome: presence and depth of vessels (via Doppler ultrasound)
cohort: 60 healthy, afebrile women aged 20-68 years with a BMI ranging from 18.5-44 kg/m2 were recruited.
finding: Cutaneous 'perforator' mapping of the abdomen using infrared thermography is feasible, and the number of 'hot spots' (indicating perfusion) was not influenced by BMI or abdominal circumference, suggesting individual variability in vascular anatomy.
